title: namma-metro-router: a cache-conscious bi-criteria transit routing engine and a multi-feed study of when multi-objective routing is load-bearing
description:
A time-dependent, multi-label-correcting bi-criteria transit routing engine in C++17 — compressed-sparse-row graph, arena-allocated labels, a separate time-independent transfer adjacency, and a selectable second objective — together with a from-scratch RAPTOR implementation that serves both as a speed baseline and as an exactness oracle.

The research artifact is the study built on top of them: across published GTFS feeds worldwide, what fraction of origin–destination pairs actually admits a genuine time-versus-changes trade-off, and which structural property of a network predicts it? The trade-off rate is measured exactly, with RAPTOR, so it is a property of the network rather than of any search heuristic; the shipped engine's own frontier and the cost of its bounded-wait lookahead are reported alongside it.

Ships with a reproducible pipeline that fetches, checksum-pins and normalises every feed, a Docker image, and a single command that regenerates every published figure. Feed checksums are recorded because transit agencies republish feeds continuously at the same URL with no version; results either side of a moved pin are not comparable, and the artifact says so rather than hiding it.

creators.name: Rajagoli, Darshan
creators.affiliation: BITS Pilani, K. K. Birla Goa Campus

notes: Reproduce with `docker build -t namma-metro-router . && docker run --rm -v "$PWD/results:/work/results" namma-metro-router`. The structural and frequency results are deterministic given the same feeds; the latency results depend on the host CPU and its power state and are not expected to reproduce numerically.
